# PLAN — gemini-4-braincells @ Junction 2026

Audience: AI coding agents working for team members. Humans don't read this file.

Location: `/srv/junction-espoo/plan/` on the team server, deliberately OUTSIDE every git repo. NEVER copy, quote at length, or commit PLAN.md, CHALLENGES.md or DECISIONS.log into any repo (including gemini-4-braincells), issue, PR or public page. Keep it current: if you change a decision, interface, port or owner, edit this file in place and add a line to `/srv/junction-espoo/plan/DECISIONS.log`.

Status: DECIDED 2026-11-13 (Fri evening) by Justinas (organiser). Do not reopen the challenge choice.

**To-do list: `/srv/junction-espoo/plan/WIN-CHECKLIST.md`.** Everything we must or will do to win, with nobody assigned. Pick an open item, mark it in progress, tick it when done, and add new work there.

## 1. Decision

- Main challenge: **"Decode the Noise" by Hostinger** (Agentic AI Track). Full brief in `/srv/junction-espoo/plan/CHALLENGES.md`.
- Tech challenges entered:
  - Committed: **Best Use of Gemini API** (Google DeepMind), **Best Use of Nemotron** (NVIDIA), **Best agentic usecase of Oxylabs Web API**.
  - Optional (only if it is clearly part of the product): **Best Use of Context.dev**.
  - Stretch: **Best Use of Gemma** (Google DeepMind).
  - Committed (set up Fri 13 Nov, see section 11): **Best Use of Entire** (MLH). **Best Use of Codex** (OpenAI), only if someone really builds a part with Codex; decide by Saturday 12:00.
- Not entered: everything else.

## 2. Product

Name: **Shill or Chill** (decided 2026-11-13 22:42 by Justinas; replaces the working name "Noise Radar"). Tagline: "Shill or chill? We check the receipts." Tone: youthful and internet-native (stock-forum, meme-page, reels culture), but never at the cost of the honesty story.
- User-facing verdict labels map 1:1 to `clusters.status` (the DB/API values don't change): `coordinated` → 🚩 **Shill** · `likely_organic` → 😎 **Chill** · `insufficient` → 🤷 **Can't tell (yet)**.
- Wording guard: "shill" appears only in the product name, headings and the verdict label for a cluster. Evidence text describes behaviour ("31 accounts, same link, 94 s") and never calls a specific account or person "a shill": we can prove coordination, not payment or intent. The methodology page says this.
- Supporting copy (optional): "Receipts" for the evidence panel, "Certified organic" for a Chill verdict.
- Infra names stay as they are (repo `gemini-4-braincells`, `/opt/noise-radar`, `~/.config/noise-radar`, the `noise-radar.` subdomain); only user-facing text changes.

A live monitor that detects coordinated amplification (bot or campaign behaviour) on Bluesky, explains each flagged cluster with evidence, and reports its own measured error rates.

Thesis, and what we must not build: the generic "paste a post and an LLM says propaganda" tool. Most teams will build that. We detect **coordination between accounts** from behaviour signals, then use LLMs only to explain and to read media. Hostinger judges "strength and honesty of detection logic, including how you handle false positives" over UI. Every design choice should favour measurable precision, calibrated confidence and explicit abstention.

Hard requirement: deployed and running live on **Hostinger** infrastructure with a **public URL** by the end of the hackathon. If it isn't live on Hostinger, we're disqualified from the main prize.

## 3. Architecture

```
Bluesky Jetstream (public websocket, no key)
        │  posts, reposts, likes, follows (filtered collections)
        ▼
ingest ──▶ Postgres (+pgvector) ◀── eval (labelled datasets → metrics)
        │
        ▼
signals: per-window feature extraction → candidate clusters → score + confidence
        │
        ├──▶ media: Nemotron 3.5 Super VL reads images/video frames, near-duplicate media matching
        ├──▶ sources: Oxylabs /scrape linked pages + /search claim origin; Context.dev domain enrichment (optional)
        ▼
analyst: Gemini writes an evidence-based verdict per cluster, or abstains
        ▼
api (FastAPI) ──▶ web dashboard (public URL on Hostinger)
```

### Components and responsibilities

| Dir | Component | Tech | Does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ingest/` | Jetstream consumer | Python 3.12, `websockets` | Subscribes to Bluesky Jetstream (VERIFY current public endpoint, e.g. `wss://jetstream2.us-east.bsky.network/subscribe?wantedCollections=app.bsky.feed.post&wantedCollections=app.bsky.feed.repost&wantedCollections=app.bsky.graph.follow`). Normalises events into `posts`, `reposts`, `follows`. Fetches profile metadata (handle, created_at, follower counts) lazily via the public AppView XRPC (`app.bsky.actor.getProfile`, VERIFY host). Optional language/keyword filter to keep volume sane. Must survive reconnects (store the cursor). |
| `signals/` | Coordination detector | Python, numpy/scikit-learn, `datasketch` (MinHash) or pgvector embeddings | Sliding windows (e.g. 10 min / 1 h). Signals: near-duplicate text across distinct accounts (MinHash/embedding similarity), burst synchrony (many accounts posting the same link or text within seconds), account freshness (created recently), shared-link concentration, repost-ring structure (the same accounts reposting each other), handle and name templating patterns, posting-time regularity. Builds candidate clusters (graph connected components or DBSCAN over account-behaviour vectors). Outputs a score in [0,1] with per-signal contributions. **Abstains** below a minimum evidence threshold. |
| `media/` | Nemotron media reader | NVIDIA API (OpenAI-compatible) | For posts with images or video in candidate clusters: describes and extracts text (OCR) from memes and screenshots; finds the same media or message reused across accounts; flags manipulated-context cues. Results feed `signals` as an extra similarity channel and go into the evidence shown to users. |
| `sources/` | Source checking | Oxylabs Web API (`/search`, `/scrape`); Context.dev (optional) | For a cluster's top shared links or claims: scrape the linked page (Oxylabs `/scrape`), search for the earliest or other sources of the claim (Oxylabs `/search`), and optionally enrich the domain (owner, age, brand) via Context.dev. Every fact shown must carry its source URL. Live calls at runtime (Oxylabs' rules: pre-downloaded data alone doesn't count). |
| `analyst/` | Explanation agent | Gemini API (function calling + JSON output) | Per cluster: given signal contributions, sample posts, media findings and source checks, write a short verdict: `coordinated` / `likely organic` / `insufficient evidence`, with confidence, the 3-5 strongest pieces of evidence, the strongest counter-evidence (why it might be organic), and what would change the verdict. It must not invent evidence: it may only cite items passed in. |
| `eval/` | Honesty and metrics | Python | Runs the detector on labelled data and reports precision, recall, F1, false-positive rate and a calibration curve, on held-out data. Results are served by the API and shown on the dashboard ("How accurate are we?"). Also a hand-labelled sample of ~100 live Bluesky clusters (two labellers, agreement reported). |
| `api/` | Backend | FastAPI | Serves clusters, evidence, metrics, health. Schema in §5. |
| `web/` | Dashboard | Vite + React + TypeScript (or plain HTML if short on time) | Live cluster feed, cluster detail page (accounts, timeline, evidence, analyst verdict, counter-evidence, sources), metrics page, "methodology and limits" page. Mobile-usable. |
| `deploy/` | Hostinger deploy | Docker Compose on a Hostinger VPS, Caddy for HTTPS | One `docker compose up -d` brings up ingest, signals worker, api, web, Postgres. Public URL plus a health check. |

### Model use

- **Gemini** (use the current best Gemini model available on the API for `analyst`, and a Flash-class one for cheap batch steps). Required for the Gemini prize: Gemini is central (it writes every verdict and runs tool calls into `sources`).
- **Nemotron 3.5 Super VL** (`nvidia/nemotron-3.5-super-vl-120b-a12b`; VERIFY the exact id on build.nvidia.com). Base URL `https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1`, OpenAI-compatible. The prize REQUIRES Super VL specifically, in core functionality and visible in the demo, plus a text explanation in the submission form (model, what it does, why it matters, how we improved its outputs). Track prompt and schema iterations and eval numbers for that text. Free tier is about 40 req/min per key: every teammate uses their own key; retries with exponential backoff; cache results by media hash.
- **Gemma** (stretch): a small fine-tuned text classifier as a cheap first-pass filter before the expensive models. Only after everything protected works.

### Data for evaluation (VERIFY availability and licence before relying on any)
- Bot detection: Cresci-2017 / other datasets from the Bot Repository (botometer.osome.iu.edu/bot-repository), TwiBot-22 (may need an access request).
- Propaganda techniques in text: SemEval-2020 Task 11 (PTC corpus), SemEval-2023 Task 3 (multilingual persuasion techniques).
- Coordination on Bluesky: no public labelled set we know of. Inject a **synthetic campaign** (scripted accounts in an offline replay, never posted to the real network) into a recorded Jetstream slice to measure recall, and hand-label live clusters to measure precision.
- Never post to Bluesky or create real accounts for testing. Analysis is read-only.

**Live deploy (2026-11-13):** https://noise-radar.srv2159172.hstgr.cloud on Hostinger VPS `srv2159172.hstgr.cloud` (KVM 2, Ubuntu 24.04, 2 vCPU / 8 GB / 96 GB). Hostinger's Docker Manager preinstalled Traefik (owns :80/:443, Let's Encrypt) and a "Hermes Agent" app; leave both alone. Our Caddy sits behind Traefik (`deploy/docker-compose.hostinger.yml`). Deploy = `deploy/deploy.sh [ref]` from the team server as `dev` (SSH alias `hostinger`, root, key `~/.ssh/hostinger_ed25519`); releases in `/opt/noise-radar/releases/<sha>`, secrets only in `/opt/noise-radar/.env` on the VPS (owners add their API keys there, then redeploy). `/version.txt` = deployed sha. Owner: Justinas.

## 4. Protected scope vs stretch

Protected (must ship, in this order):
1. Jetstream ingest → Postgres, running continuously.
2. Coordination signals + clusters with a score, per-signal contributions and abstention.
3. Gemini analyst verdicts with evidence and counter-evidence.
4. Nemotron Super VL in the pipeline on real media, visible in the cluster view.
5. Oxylabs live `/scrape` + `/search` on cluster links, with URLs shown.
6. Eval page with precision and FP rate on held-out data.
7. Live on Hostinger at a public URL.

Stretch: Context.dev enrichment, Gemma first-pass filter, calibration curve, site-owner webhook/alerts, multilingual (Finnish) support, CRACI CI.

## 5. Shared interfaces (contract; change only with a note here and in DECISIONS.log)

Postgres tables (minimum columns):
- `accounts(did PK, handle, display_name, created_at, followers, follows, first_seen)`
- `posts(uri PK, did FK, text, langs[], created_at, reply_to, embed_kind, embed_urls[], media_hashes[], ingested_at)`
- `reposts(uri PK, did, subject_uri, created_at)`; `follows(uri PK, did, subject_did, created_at)`
- `clusters(id PK, window_start, window_end, score, confidence, status /*coordinated|likely_organic|insufficient*/ , signals JSONB, created_at, updated_at)`
- `cluster_members(cluster_id, did, role)`; `cluster_posts(cluster_id, post_uri)`
- `evidence(id PK, cluster_id, kind /*signal|media|source|analyst*/, summary, detail JSONB, source_url, model, created_at)`
- `eval_runs(id PK, dataset, split, precision, recall, f1, fpr, n, details JSONB, created_at)`
- Added 2026-11-13 by kirill (migration `db/migrations/002_ingest_signals.sql`, applied with `python -m common.migrate`; additive except that the raw tables are recreated while empty):
  - Raw tables `posts`, `reposts`, `likes` (new), `follows` are partitioned BY HOUR on `seen_at` (Jetstream server time, from time_us); PK is `(uri, seen_at)`. `created_at` stays the record's client timestamp. Every raw row has `seen_at` and `deleted_at` (deletes are soft). Retention drops old raw partitions (env `INGEST_RETENTION_HOURS`, `INGEST_LIKES_RETENTION_HOURS`). Anything a cluster references must be copied to `cluster_posts_snapshot` / `evidence` (signals does this).
  - `posts` + `cid, reply_root, quote_uri, mentions[], tags[], text_hash`; `media_hashes[]` = image/video blob CIDs; `embed_urls[]` = external card + link facets, normalised (`signals/textnorm.py`). `reposts`/`likes` + `subject_did`.
  - `likes(uri, did, subject_uri, subject_did, created_at, seen_at, deleted_at)`.
  - `accounts` + `did_created_at, pds_host, handle_changes, status, status_at, posts_count, description_len, has_avatar, profile_fetched_at, plc_fetched_at`.
  - `account_events(id, did, kind account|identity, active, status, handle, seq, time_us, event_time, received_at)`: takedowns etc. from Jetstream, stored from the first minute.
  - `ingest_state(stream PK, cursor_time_us, host, last_event_at, events_per_s, updated_at)`.
  - `campaigns(id, first_seen, last_seen, latest_cluster_id, max_score, status)`; `clusters` + `campaign_id, p_value, families_fired, detector_version, window_kind, size, synthetic`.
  - `cluster_posts_snapshot` (copies of posts referenced by clusters; outlives retention); `schema_migrations`.
- Added 2026-11-13 by kirill (PR #6, `signals/README.md` has the exact JSON): `clusters.signals` JSONB = `{detector_version, score, family_scores{content,timing,network,identity}, families_fired[], p_value, null_model{...}, organic_guard_score, signals[{family,name,score,polarity for|against,summary,evidence_id}], status_rule}`. `evidence(kind='signal')` = one row per signal/guard, upserted by name (ids stable while a cluster updates); `detail` has `post_uris`, `post_urls` (bsky.app), `dids`, `profile_urls` plus signal numbers; `model='detector:<version>'`. One `clusters` row per episode (updated in place while the same accounts keep going; check `updated_at`), `campaign_id` links episodes. Status is decided by the detector's rules, not by the LLM.
- PROPOSAL (kirill -> Temuulen/Justinas, NOT decided): the analyst should explain the detector's status instead of deciding it. Keep `status` in the verdict JSON equal to `clusters.status`, and add `llm_assessment` (`coordinated|likely_organic|insufficient`) + `agrees_with_detector` (bool) + `disagreement_reason`. Disagreements are shown in the UI and counted in eval, so "why coordinated?" is never answered with "the LLM said so".

API (FastAPI, JSON):
- `GET /api/health` → `{ok, ingest_lag_s, last_event_at}`
- `GET /api/clusters?status=&min_score=&limit=` → list of cluster summaries
- `GET /api/clusters/{id}` → cluster + members + posts sample + evidence + analyst verdict
- `GET /api/metrics` → latest `eval_runs` per dataset
- `POST /api/analyze` `{text? , url? , handle?}` → ad-hoc check for judges trying their own input (returns signals if the account/post is in our window, otherwise "insufficient evidence" plus text-level findings, clearly labelled as weaker)

Analyst verdict JSON (stored in `evidence.detail` with `kind='analyst'`):
```json
{"status": "coordinated|likely_organic|insufficient", "confidence": 0.0,
 "evidence": [{"evidence_id": 1, "why": "..."}],
 "counter_evidence": ["..."], "would_change_verdict": ["..."], "model": "gemini-..."}
```

## 6. Team, ownership, ports

|---|---|---|
| Justinas (`dev`) | Hostinger deploy, `eval/`, submission texts, pitch, final say on scope | 3000-3009, 8000-8009 |
| Kirill (`kirill`) | `ingest/`, `signals/`, DB schema | 3010-3019, 8010-8019 |
| Temuulen (`temuulen`) | `analyst/` (Gemini), `sources/` (Oxylabs, Context.dev), `api/` | 3020-3029, 8020-8029 |
| Valtteri (`valtteri`) | `media/` (Nemotron), `web/` dashboard | 3030-3039, 8030-8039 |

Ownership means "decides and reviews", not "only one who may touch". Coordinate through commits (code) and this file (plan). Run `je status` / `je log` before starting. Use your own port block only.

## 7. Working rules for agents

- Work in your person's worktree: `je wt gemini-4-braincells <task>` (branch `<user>/<task>`). Merge `main` (`origin/main`) in often. To land work: push your branch, open a GitHub PR, and **squash-merge** it (`gh pr merge --squash`), then `git pull` in the main checkout. ## Workflow with Entire

- One Trail per feature: from your feature branch run `entire trail create --title "<what and why>" --type feature`. Commits pushed to that branch, and the agent sessions behind them, attach to the Trail.
- Commit agent work with the agent running, so Entire links the commit to its session (`Entire-Checkpoint:` trailer). Don't amend or rebase away those trailers.
- Before merging, run `entire review general`. It reviews locally with Claude Code (no Entire credit; Codex-only users ask a teammate to run it) and posts the verdict to the Trail. Fix or dismiss each finding, then open the PR with `entire trail ci-pr`, undraft it with `entire trail ready`, and squash-merge it while keeping the checkpoint trailers in the squash commit:

  ```bash
  gh pr merge <n> --squash --body "$(git log --format='%(trailers:key=Entire-Checkpoint)' origin/main..HEAD | grep . | sort -u)"
  ```

  A squash without those trailers loses the link between the commit on `main` and its agent sessions.
- Don't run `entire trail rerun-review` or enable project Agents on entire.com: those run paid cloud agents. Ask the repo owner first.
- Never paste keys or `.env` contents into a prompt: transcripts are stored in checkpoints.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Ship a committed git ref to the Hostinger VPS and (re)start the stack there.
#   deploy/deploy.sh [ref]          # default: origin/main (run `git fetch` first)
# Env: HOSTINGER_HOST (required), HOSTINGER_USER (default root), HOSTINGER_SSH_KEY (optional key file),
#      HOSTINGER_DIR (default /opt/noise-radar).
# The VPS needs no GitHub access: the tree goes over SSH with `git archive`, so only committed files
# ship. Each deploy lands in $DIR/releases/<sha>, `current` points at it, and $DIR/.env (created once
# by hand on the VPS, never committed) is linked into every release. Roll back: deploy an older sha.
set -euo pipefail

ref=${1:-origin/main}
host=${HOSTINGER_HOST:?set HOSTINGER_HOST}
user=${HOSTINGER_USER:-root}
dir=${HOSTINGER_DIR:-/opt/noise-radar}
ssh_opts=(-o BatchMode=yes)
if [[ -n ${HOSTINGER_SSH_KEY:-} ]]; then ssh_opts+=(-i "$HOSTINGER_SSH_KEY" -o IdentitiesOnly=yes); fi

sha=$(git rev-parse --short=12 "$ref^{commit}")
echo "deploying $ref ($sha) to $user@$host:$dir"

# 1) upload the tree into releases/<sha>.tmp, unless that release is already on the VPS
if ssh "${ssh_opts[@]}" "$user@$host" "test -d '$dir/releases/$sha'"; then
  echo "release $sha already on the VPS, skipping upload"
else
  git archive --format=tar "$sha" | ssh "${ssh_opts[@]}" "$user@$host" \
    "set -e; rm -rf '$dir/releases/$sha.tmp'; mkdir -p '$dir/releases/$sha.tmp'; tar -x -C '$dir/releases/$sha.tmp'"
fi

# 2) build, start, and only then point `current` at it
ssh "${ssh_opts[@]}" "$user@$host" bash -s -- "$dir" "$sha" <<'REMOTE'
set -euo pipefail
dir=$1 sha=$2
rel=$dir/releases/$sha
test -f "$dir/.env" || { echo "missing $dir/.env on the VPS (copy .env.example and fill it in)" >&2; exit 1; }
exec 9>"$dir/.deploy.lock"
flock -w 600 9 || { echo "another deploy is running" >&2; exit 1; }
if [[ -d $rel.tmp ]]; then
  ln -sfn ../../.env "$rel.tmp/.env"
  echo "$sha" > "$rel.tmp/web/public/version.txt"
  rm -rf "$rel" && mv "$rel.tmp" "$rel"
fi
touch "$rel"   # newest mtime, so pruning below never removes the live release
# Run compose from the real release path (not the `current` symlink): bind-mount paths then change
# per release, so compose recreates the containers that mount repo files (Caddy, db init script).
cd "$rel"
dc=(docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml -f deploy/docker-compose.hostinger.yml --env-file .env)
"${dc[@]}" build
"${dc[@]}" up -d --remove-orphans
ln -sfn "releases/$sha" "$dir/current"
docker image prune -f --filter label=com.docker.compose.project=noise-radar >/dev/null
# keep the 5 newest finished releases
ls -1dt "$dir"/releases/*/ | { grep -v '\.tmp/$' || true; } | tail -n +6 | xargs -r rm -rf
"${dc[@]}" ps
REMOTE

"""Gemini as the verdict model: structured JSON output against the VerdictDraft schema."""

import logging
import time
from typing import Protocol

from google import genai
from google.genai import types

from analyst.verdict import VerdictDraft
from common.config import get_settings

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class VerdictModel(Protocol):
    name: str

    def draft(self, system: str, prompt: str) -> VerdictDraft: ...


class GeminiVerdictModel:
    def __init__(self, api_key: str, model: str, *, temperature: float = 0.2):
        if not api_key:
            raise ValueError("GEMINI_API_KEY is not set")
        self._client = genai.Client(api_key=api_key)
        self.name = model
        self._temperature = temperature

    @classmethod
    def from_settings(cls) -> "GeminiVerdictModel":
        s = get_settings()
        return cls(s.gemini_api_key, s.gemini_model)

    def draft(self, system: str, prompt: str) -> VerdictDraft:
        started = time.monotonic()
        res = self._client.models.generate_content(
            model=self.name,
            contents=prompt,
            config=types.GenerateContentConfig(
                system_instruction=system,
                response_mime_type="application/json",
                response_schema=VerdictDraft,
                temperature=self._temperature,
            ),
        )
        usage = res.usage_metadata
        log.info(
            "gemini call model=%s latency_ms=%d prompt_tokens=%s output_tokens=%s",
            self.name,
            (time.monotonic() - started) * 1000,
            getattr(usage, "prompt_token_count", None),
            getattr(usage, "candidates_token_count", None),
        )
        if isinstance(res.parsed, VerdictDraft):
            return res.parsed
        return VerdictDraft.model_validate_json(res.text or "")

"""FastAPI backend. Routes and their JSON shapes are listed in README.md (Shared interfaces)."""

import logging
from datetime import UTC, datetime

from fastapi import FastAPI

from api.routes import analyze, clusters, metrics
from common.db import connect

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(name)s %(message)s")

app = FastAPI(title="Noise Radar API", version="0.2.0")
app.include_router(clusters.router)
app.include_router(metrics.router)
app.include_router(analyze.router)


@app.get("/api/health")
def health() -> dict:
    """{ok, ingest_lag_s, last_event_at}. ok=false (not an error) when the DB is unreachable."""
    try:
        with connect() as conn:
            row = conn.execute("SELECT max(ingested_at) AS last FROM posts").fetchone()
    except Exception as exc:  # DB down or schema missing: report it, don't crash the probe
        return {
            "ok": False,
            "ingest_lag_s": None,
            "last_event_at": None,
            "error": type(exc).__name__,
        }

    last = row["last"] if row else None
    lag = (datetime.now(UTC) - last).total_seconds() if last else None
    return {
        "ok": True,
        "ingest_lag_s": round(lag, 1) if lag is not None else None,
        "last_event_at": last.isoformat() if last else None,
    }

# One Python image for every backend service (api, ingest, signals worker...). Pick the command in compose.
FROM ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:python3.12-bookworm-slim

WORKDIR /app
ENV UV_COMPILE_BYTECODE=1 UV_LINK_MODE=copy PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1

COPY pyproject.toml uv.lock README.md ./
RUN uv sync --frozen --no-dev --no-install-project

COPY . .
RUN uv sync --frozen --no-dev

ENV PATH="/app/.venv/bin:$PATH"
CMD ["uvicorn", "api.main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000"]
## Deploy

Live at **https://noise-radar.srv2159172.hstgr.cloud** (Hostinger VPS, Ubuntu 24.04, Docker).
The VPS's Docker Manager already runs Traefik on :80/:443 with Let's Encrypt, so our Caddy sits
behind it (`deploy/docker-compose.hostinger.yml`). From any checkout with the deploy SSH key:

```bash
git fetch && HOSTINGER_HOST=srv2159172.hstgr.cloud HOSTINGER_SSH_KEY=REDACTED \
  deploy/deploy.sh                      # default ref: origin/main; pass a sha to roll back
curl https://noise-radar.srv2159172.hstgr.cloud/api/health
curl https://noise-radar.srv2159172.hstgr.cloud/version.txt   # deployed commit
```

`deploy.sh` ships the committed tree with `git archive` (the VPS has no GitHub access) into
`/opt/noise-radar/releases/<sha>`, points `current` at it and runs compose. Secrets live only in
`/opt/noise-radar/.env` on the VPS (same names as `.env.example`); edit it there, then redeploy.

On a plain VPS without Traefik, drop the override and set `PUBLIC_DOMAIN` so Caddy gets HTTPS itself:
`docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml --env-file .env up -d --build`.

All backend services share one image (`Dockerfile`); add a service in compose with its own

# Outside health check for the public site. Exit 0 = healthy; prints one line either way.
#   deploy/check.sh [base-url]      # default https://noise-radar.srv2159172.hstgr.cloud
# Env: MAX_LAG_S (default 300): /api/health fails when the newest ingested post is older than this.
set -uo pipefail

url=${1:-https://noise-radar.srv2159172.hstgr.cloud}
max_lag=${MAX_LAG_S:-300}
fail=()
get() { curl -fsS --max-time 20 "$url$1"; }

health=$(get /api/health) || fail+=("/api/health unreachable")
if [[ -n ${health:-} ]]; then
  python3 -c 'import json,sys; h=json.loads(sys.argv[1]); lag=h.get("ingest_lag_s"); sys.exit(0 if h.get("ok") and lag is not None and lag < float(sys.argv[2]) else 1)' \
    "$health" "$max_lag" || fail+=("health not ok: $health")
fi
for path in /api/clusters?limit=1 /api/metrics /; do
  get "$path" >/dev/null || fail+=("$path failed")
done
version=$(get /version.txt 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\n') || version=unknown

ts=$(date -u +%FT%TZ)
if ((${#fail[@]})); then
  echo "$ts FAIL $url version=$version: ${fail[*]}"
  exit 1
fi

EOF

The live site now runs current main, release **e0f72a2** (PR #13 on top of #8 and #11), at https://noise-radar.srv2159172.hstgr.cloud. From outside, `/api/health`, `/api/clusters`, `/api/clusters/{id}` and `/api/metrics` all return 200, but `/api/metrics` returns an empty list.

**What's live**
- All services are up with no restarts and no OOM kills: db, migrate (runs once and exits), ingest, signals, api, caddy/web, sources and analyst.
- **Sources:** live Oxylabs `/scrape` and `/search` calls return 200.
- **Analyst:** it was failing every verdict, because `gemini-2.5-pro` (the code default) returns 404 "no longer available to new users". I set `GEMINI_MODEL=gemini-4-argon` in the VPS `.env`. Verdicts are now being written, about 12 s each.
- **Signals:** the 1h pass (912k actions) finished in 230 s and used at most 2.46 GiB under the new 4G cap.

**What I changed**
1. **VPS `.env`:** copied the Gemini, NVIDIA, Oxylabs Web API, Context.dev and Verda keys file-to-file from `team.env`, without printing them. I added `GEMINI_MODEL` and the retention settings, and removed the old empty `OXYLABS_USERNAME`/`PASSWORD`. A backup is next to it as `.env.bak-*`.
2. **Signals memory (PR #13):** raised the limit from 2G to 4G (and 1.5 CPU) in `deploy/docker-compose.hostinger.yml` only. I didn't touch Kirill's code; the note to Kirill is in DECISIONS.log.
3. **Disk:** raw data is kept 48 h and likes 12 h. I measured about 0.66 GB/h of raw data, which settles at roughly 16 GB of database (about 32 GB if traffic doubles); 82 GB is free. Cluster posts are kept past retention in `cluster_posts_snapshot`. Most of the 13–14 GB in use was Docker images and build cache, so `deploy.sh` now also clears build cache older than 72 h.
4. **Health check and restarts:** every long-running service already had `restart: unless-stopped`; `migrate` stays one-shot. I added:
   - a healthcheck on the api container;
   - `deploy/check.sh`, which checks health, ingest lag, clusters, metrics, the web page and version from outside. It runs every 5 min from `dev`'s cron on the team server and logs to `~dev/noise-radar-health.log`; the first run was OK;
   - a `CHECK_URL` option in `deploy.sh` that runs the same check after a deploy;
   - the deploy and check commands in the repo README.
5. **Jetstream slices:** the eval thread had already copied Fri 19–20 UTC into `data/eval-slices/`. I created `/srv/junction-espoo/data/jetstream-kept/` with hard links to those files (no extra disk) and a README. A cron job will also copy Fri 21 UTC (busy) and Sat 09 UTC once each hour finishes. Sat 09 UTC is a guess at a quiet hour, not yet checked.
6. **PLAN, checklist, log:** the public URL and the running setup are in PLAN §12. I ticked the H items, the Jetstream item and "Put the public URL in PLAN", and added six lines to DECISIONS.log.

**Still broken or open**
- **Metrics:** the VPS database has no eval results yet, so the metrics page will show nothing until the eval thread writes its runs to production.
- **Gemini default:** `common/config.py` and `.env.example` still say `gemini-2.5-pro`, which fails. That needs a PR from the analyst owner (Temuulen, or the dev-gemini-agent thread), who should also confirm argon over carbon or hydrogen.
- **Media:** there is no media (Nemotron) worker in main yet.
- **Alerts:** the health check only writes a log; nobody is alerted when it fails.
- **Entire:** PR #13 has no checkpoint trailers, because this session isn't captured by Entire, and I skipped the Entire review and Trail steps.
